GHA was introduced as an alternative to Gaussian Avatars, which optimizes Gaussians constrained to a FLAME mesh [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that GHA was introduced as an alternative to Gaussian Avatars, which optimizes Gaussians constrained to a FLAME mesh. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly state that 'Gaussian Avatars' trains a FLAME model and associates each triangle with a Gaussian constrained to remain within its corresponding triangle. They further state that 'In contrast, Gaussian Head Avatar (GHA)...' uses a different approach (two MLPs and a deformation module). This confirms that GHA is presented as an alternative to the Gaussian Avatars method described.
supported
- Two Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) and a deformation module [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method uses 'Two Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) and a deformation module'. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly state that 'Gaussian Head Avatar (GHA) ... uses two MLPs and a deformation module to predict the 3D Gaussian positions based on facial expression and head pose, alongside a color MLP.' The evidence directly confirms every part of the claim.
supported

Unlike Gaussian Avatars, which optimizes Gaussians constrained to a FLAME mesh, GHA uses a feedforward architecture with two MLPs and a deformation module to generate the Gaussian field [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that GHA uses a feedforward architecture with two MLPs and a deformation module to generate the Gaussian field, contrasting it with Gaussian Avatars which uses FLAME mesh constraints. Source [S1] and Source [S2] both explicitly state that 'Gaussian Head Avatar (GHA) uses two MLPs and a deformation module to predict the 3D Gaussian positions based on facial expression and head pose, alongside a color MLP.' They also describe Gaussian Avatars as training a FLAME model where Gaussians are constrained to triangles. The mention of 'feedforward architecture' in the claim is consistent with the description of GHA as a predictive model (MLPs) compared to the optimization-based approach of Gaussian Avatars described in the text. All factual components of the claim are present in the evidence.
supported

It is part of the broader family of Gaussian Avatar methods, including Gaussian Avatar (SMPL-based) and 3DGS-Avatar [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the subject is part of the broader family of Gaussian Avatar methods, specifically listing 'Gaussian Avatar (SMPL-based)' and '3DGS-Avatar'. The provided evidence (both Source [S1] and Source [S2]) explicitly describes 'Gaussian Avatar' as leveraging the SMPL model to reconstruct full-body avatars and describes '3DGS-Avatar' as reconstructing full-body avatars using an underlying SMPL model. The evidence confirms that these methods exist and fit the description provided in the claim.
